title: Thin-client action lifecycle and debuggable handshake PRD
body:
Overview:

This doc proposes a compact, observable protocol for thin-client interactions with the Hosted API when using streaming responses + tool calling + structured output. The goal is a small, opinionated handshake and per-action lifecycle that makes SDKs easy to implement and gives developers deterministic hooks to debug, resume, and reason about partial results.

Context / problem:
- Customers building interactive UIs (mobile widgets, web compositors, IDE assistants) need low-latency partial outputs but also robust tool invocation semantics (idempotency, rollback, developer-visible state).
- Existing streaming contracts leak implementation details to callers and make client-side resumption, testing, and error diagnosis hard. SDKs end up implementing bespoke heuristics for retries, backpressure, and tool-call confirmation.
- We need a small set of server-side guarantees and a compact handshake that enables simple client semantics: resume-from-checkpoint, explicit partial-commit, traceable tool invocation, and typed structured output.

Goals (success metrics):
- Developer ergonomics: client integration work decreased by 40% in a sample integration (internal developer study).
- Observability: tool call and partial-commit events show up in trace view with >95% fidelity to what client sees.
- Reliability: accidental duplicate tool executions reduced by 90% via commit token semantics and idempotency keys.
- Latency: incremental partial outputs delivered within existing streaming p95 budgets (no regression).

Non-goals:
- This is not a full transactional system for distributed state changes. We provide primitives for safe tool invocation but not multi-step distributed rollback across customer tool backends.
- Not addressing long-living session storage (separate feature area).

User personas and scenarios:
- Mobile product engineer: wants deterministic UI updates and ability to resume a partially-rendered assistant flow after a network hiccup.
- Backend platform engineer: wants to correlate API traces with tool call logs to reconcile billing and debugging.
- Solutions engineer: needs consistent structured output for enterprise connectors and clear rollback semantics when a downstream tool fails.

High-level proposal (summary):
1) Compact handshake at session start: client opens a streaming request with minimal metadata (client_id, sdk_version, optional resume_token). Server responds with a session_token and initial schema pointers.
2) Frame model: use small typed frames (meta, text_delta, structured_delta, tool_invoke, tool_ack, commit, checkpoint). Every frame carries a monotonic frame_id and optional parent_id for logical grouping.
3) Commit tokens + idempotency: tool_invoke frames include idempotency_key and expected_commit_token. The server only marks a tool execution 'committed' when it sees the matching commit frame or an automatic commit policy triggers after success.
4) Checkpoints for resume: checkpoints are lightweight snapshots (checkpoint_id) that clients can use to resume a stream without re-running tool calls.
5) SDK ergonomics: client libraries provide thin abstractions (onDelta, onToolEvent, requestCheckpoint, resumeFrom) and default backpressure heuristics.

Low-level contract (frames):
- meta: session metadata, model variant served, feature flags, initial validation errors. Fields: frame_id, type=meta, payload: freeform map.
- text_delta: incremental plain text token/patch. Fields: frame_id, parent_id?, content_fragment, stable_flag (boolean).
- structured_delta: JSON/YAML-safe partial structured output. Fields: frame_id, parent_id?, json_patch (RFC 6902-ish), schema_version.
- tool_invoke: request to run a tool. Fields: frame_id, parent_id?, tool_name, args_serialized, idempotency_key, expect_commit_after (optional policy).
- tool_ack: acknowledgement of invocation delivered by the runtime (not necessarily execution). Fields: frame_id, ref_id (tool_invoke.frame_id), status=queued|running.
- tool_result: actual result emitted by tool provider or runtime. Fields: frame_id, ref_id, status=ok|error, output_serialized, provenance (optional URL or id).
- commit: marks logical commit of a prior operation or tool result. Fields: frame_id, target_ref_id (the thing being committed), commit_token (opaque), rhyme: auto|manual.
- checkpoint: lightweight resume point. Fields: frame_id, checkpoint_id, included_refs (list of frame ids), checksum.

Handshake sequence (example):
- Client POST /v1/responses?stream=true with headers {X-Client:web-embed, X-SDK:thin-js/0.3.1}. Body: {prompt, features:["tool-calls","structured-output"], resume_token:null}
- Server responds status 200 then emits meta frame: frame_id=1 {session_token:"S-321", schema_anchor:"/schemas/assistant-v2"}
- Server streams text_delta frames as model generates. When model decides to request a tool, server emits tool_invoke frame with suggested args and idempotency_key.
- SDK receives tool_invoke and either: 1) auto-proxy (server-side plugin) or 2) client proxies: SDK emits an HTTP call to customer tool endpoint and returns tool_result frames into the stream using a local SDK helper which posts results back to a control endpoint.
- Once tool_result is accepted, server issues commit frame referencing tool_result.

Thin-client proxy pattern (an ergonomics option):
- Many mobile clients cannot reliably host a webhook. Provide 'proxy-mode' where the SDK handles tool invocation locally and streams result back to the control-plane via a short-lived upload endpoint. This avoids forcing clients to run servers while preserving idempotency keys and commit tokens.
- Security: uploads must be signed with session_token and ephemeral upload token.

SDK ergonomics (detailed):
- JS, Python, and Swift SDKs expose the same surface:
  - startStream(request): returns StreamHandle
  - StreamHandle.on('delta', (d) => {})
  - StreamHandle.on('tool', (invoke)=> { return handleTool(invoke) }) // handler may return promise for result or null to allow server-side proxy
  - StreamHandle.requestCheckpoint(): Promise<checkpoint_id>
  - StreamHandle.resumeFrom(checkpoint_id, resume_options)
- Default behavior: SDK will auto-ack tool_acks and buffer tool_result until commit is received unless user opts into optimistic-apply.
- Backpressure: SDK exposes suggested read-window (in bytes or frames) which servers use to throttle generation; clients may set read_window to smaller values to keep UI responsive.
- Debug hooks: enable verbose mode where SDK logs frame stream to local dev console with trace ids. This is gated behind sdk_version flag to avoid shipping to production apps by default.

Developer UX and debugging features:
- Trace ids: every request has a trace_id surfaced to SDK and added to every frame; trace spans are linkable to console traces and commit events.
- Replay kit: SDK can request a transcript of last N frames and full checkpoints for offline reproductions (admin-only, subject to retention).
- Deterministic playback: SDK can 'replay' frames locally by applying structured_delta patches and tool_result stubs to validate UI renderers.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit span events for: session_start, tool_invoke_sent, tool_result_received, commit_seen, checkpoint_written, resume.
- Logs include frame counts, average frame size, and % of sessions using proxy-mode.
- SLOs: measure time between tool_invoke and commit and alert when p95 > 2s for common tool types.

Security and privacy:
- Tool args marked as sensitive will not be stored in persistent checkpoints; only hashed provenance retained.
- Checkpoints are encrypted at rest and scoped to session_token.
- Proxy-mode uploads are one-time-use with short TTL and require session signing.

Compatibility / migration notes:
- Back-compat: old non-framed streaming will continue to work; new clients opt-in by setting features:["framed-handshake"].
- Migration plan: roll out framed-handshake behind feature flag; stage A: internal SDK + partner integrations; stage B: opt-in public beta; stage C: default for new SDK versions.

Rollout plan and experiments:
- Canary cohort: 5 internal teams + 3 enterprise partners (low-latency chat and code-assistant). Measure integration time and error rates.
- Experiment A: optimistic-apply off vs on to measure perceived latency vs mismatch rate.
- Experiment B: proxy-mode vs webhook-mode for mobile clients to compare developer effort and reliability.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How large should checkpoints be? Trade-off between resume fidelity and storage/IO cost. Suggest default of only including committed frames and last N text_delta frames.
- Commit semantics for multi-tool micro-transactions: do we provide group-commit primitives or rely on client-side orchestration? Proposal: add commit.group_id in next iteration if demand surfaces.
- Failure model: if commit never arrives, when does server mark tool as failed and surface SLA to client? Proposal: server-side commit-timeout policy per tool (configurable).

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: prototype wire format and JS SDK patch (ENG-1423).
- Product: draft public beta messaging and example integrations for mobile (PRD owner to draft).
- Research: evaluate memory cost of checkpointing on low-latency hosts and quantify expected storage delta for top-20 customers.
- Security: review proxy upload signing flow and update threat model.

Notes to self / work-in-progress items:
- Need example sequence diagrams and sample SDK code for both proxy-mode and webhook-mode.
- Build a minimal playback utility to validate structured_delta patches across SDKs.
- Draft docs page: "Framed streaming handshake" with examples and troubleshooting checklist.
